- A flaky file that passes on retry gives green-with-flakes and a flake-log row.

## PREP
Acceptance: the drain pass no longer runs a second full paged open-PR listing inside the listing step; what merges is unchanged.
Acceptance: the heavy-field seed read is cache-only, bounded by the snapshot TTL and dirty rule, so it never calls gh and never refreshes.
Pre-mortem: a stale or dirty snapshot gives no seed, so the live listing hydrates body and files as before (more gh reads, no wrong merge).
Pre-mortem: the open set still comes from the live listing, not the seed, so no blocker or sibling can be missed.
Files: scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs (seed read), scripts/lib/pr-snapshot.mjs (cache-only skips the stale-ok window), scripts/lib/__tests__/pr-snapshot.test.mjs.
Tests: scripts/lib/__tests__/pr-snapshot.test.mjs and pr-snapshot-stale-ok.test.mjs (69 pass); verify-lane green.

## Why
Recent drain passes took 490-710 s (against 130-230 s overnight). The pass timing line shows listing at 125-300 s, of which `listing.seed` was 60-200 s. The seed was a fresh-or-refresh read of the shared snapshot, so a stale snapshot ran a whole paged listing, and then the pass paged the same PRs again (`listing.pages`, about 50 s). The seed only fills body and files and is used only when updatedAt and head SHA match the live row.

## Residual risk
Seeded heavy fields keep the existing restamp behaviour in the paged listing (seed rows count as fresh when used); this change does not alter it and the seed age bound is the same snapshot TTL as before.
Gains depend on other daemons keeping the snapshot fresh; when they do not, the seed is empty and only selected PRs hydrate.

Audit: NOT WEAKENED on the final sha (earlier rounds fixed: dirty rule, stale-ok window, age bound).

## Overlay stale detector (PR1 of overlay-prune v2): detect and alert, no removal

Stale overlays that conflict with main kept looping daemon rebuilds. This adds a post-plan detector that never removes anything.

- `overlay-prune.mjs` (new): counts consecutive main-conflicts per (ref, tip, registration) for pr:0, PR-less, unpinned overlays. After more than 2, it emits one `overlay-stale-conflict` event plus a needs-you notice with the exact owner action. It also reports supersession, judged on the sha in `plan.applied`, never the fetched tip. Unknown state is kept and alerted once. A static test asserts the file has no removal API.
- `prepare.mjs` / `adopt.mjs`: a pending (or unreadable) drop intent now blocks any build that changes the registration set, at planning, at removal (under the add-guard lock) and at finalize (whole finalize under the add-guard lock). Recovery and health-watch rollback still run. A refused removal stops the build for replanning.
- `daemon-overlay.mjs stale [--json]`: read-only listing. `rebuild.mjs`: two new reasons classified as failures. Settings: `overlayStale` with `WE_OVERLAY_STALE=0` override.
- Live proof: `stale --json` on the five daemon clones returns `[]` (the detector has not run there yet, so no overlay qualifies).

## Known older-code findings (R1052 ratchet)
The canonical audit returns WEAKENED on older paths this PR does not weaken; each reproduces on origin/main (it has no add-guard lock or drop-pending check at all). Carded as PR2 follow-ups: swap cleanup without the add-guard lock; finalize not revalidating registrations against the plan; `dropSuspectOverlays` removing by ref without `expectedOverlay`; edge-fetch treating a single fetch failure as a deleted branch. Waiver requests recorded under R1052.
